# kangaroo_cache_repro.ipynb

## [markdown]

# Reproducing Kangaroo (SOSP '21) on Chameleon — Simulator Path

Adapts the Chameleon baremetal experiment pattern to reproduce a result from
*"Kangaroo: Caching Billions of Tiny Objects on Flash"* (McAllister et al.,
SOSP 2021, [paper](https://www.pdl.cmu.edu/PDL-FTP/NVM/McAllister-SOSP21.pdf))
using the **trace-driven simulator** the paper authors built — not the on-flash
CacheLib version.

Why the simulator and not the on-flash code:
- The paper itself (§6) says "we implemented a trace-driven cache simulator for
  Kangaroo" to explore parameters. The simulator is what produced the parameter
  sweeps in Figures 8, 9, 11, 12.
- Build is ~30 seconds (plain C++, no external deps) vs ~30–60 min for the
  CacheLib fork (folly, fizz, fbthrift, …).
- No raw flash device needed → `compute_cascadelake` (the original notebook's
  node type) is fine.
- Simulator output is deterministic given a config — easy to eyeball against
  the paper's figures.

What this notebook produces: one Kangaroo-vs-SA miss-ratio comparison figure on
a synthetic Zipf workload (α=0.9, matching the paper's Zipf sensitivity study).
The shape should match the paper: Kangaroo and SA achieve similar miss ratios,
but Kangaroo writes much less to flash.

Driver repo: https://github.com/saramcallister/Kangaroo

## [markdown]

## 1. Configure Chameleon site + project

## [code]

```python
from chi import context

context.version = "1.0"
context.choose_site(default="CHI@TACC")
context.choose_project()
```

## [markdown]

## 2. Pick a node

`compute_cascadelake` works fine — the simulator is CPU-only, no flash device
needed.

<!-- 1 cell(s) omitted: no provisioning -->

## [markdown]

## 3. Reserve the node

3 hours is plenty: build is ~30s, a small Zipf simulator sweep is ~10–30 min.

## [code]

```python
from chi import lease
from datetime import timedelta
import os

my_lease = lease.Lease(
    f"{os.getenv('USER')}-kangaroo-sim",
    duration=timedelta(hours=3),
)
my_lease.add_node_reservation(nodes=[available_nodes[0]])
my_lease.add_fip_reservation(1)
my_lease.submit(idempotent=True)
```

## [markdown]

## 4. Launch server

## [code]

```python
from chi import server

my_server = server.Server(
    f"{os.getenv('USER')}-kangaroo-sim",
    reservation_id=my_lease.node_reservations[0]["id"],
    image_name="CC-Ubuntu22.04",
)
my_server.submit(idempotent=True)
```
